title: Computational profiling of hiPSC-derived heart organoids reveals chamber defects associated with NKX2-5 deficiency.
authors: Feng, Wei; Schriever, Hannah; Jiang, Shan; Bais, Abha; Wu, Haodi; Kostka, Dennis; Li, Guang
one_liner_zh: 该文利用机器学习标签转移分析hiPSC来源心脏类器官中NKX2-5缺陷导致的腔室缺陷，核心是心脏发育与疾病建模，而非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合机制研究。
abstract: Heart organoids have the potential to generate primary heart-like anatomical structures and hold great promise as in vitro models for cardiac disease. However, their properties have not yet been fully studied, which hinders their wide spread application. Here we report the development of differentiation systems for ventricular and atrial heart organoids, enabling the study of heart diseases with chamber defects. We show that our systems generate chamber-specific organoids comprising of the major cardiac cell types, and we use single cell RNA sequencing together with sample multiplexing to characterize the cells we generate. To that end, we developed a machine learning label transfer approach leveraging cell type, chamber, and laterality annotations available for primary human fetal heart cells. We then used this model to analyze organoid cells from an isogeneic line carrying an Ebstein's anomaly associated genetic variant in NKX2-5, and we successfully recapitulated the disease's atrialized ventricular defects. In summary, we have established a workflow integrating heart organoids and computational analysis to model heart development in normal and disease states.
abstract_zh: 心脏类器官（heart organoids）具有生成类似初级心脏解剖结构的潜力，并作为心脏疾病的体外模型展现出广阔前景。然而，其特性尚未被充分研究，这阻碍了其广泛应用。在此，我们报告了心室和心房心脏类器官分化系统的开发，从而能够研究伴有腔室缺陷的心脏疾病。我们证明，我们的系统能够生成包含主要心脏细胞类型的腔室特异性类器官，并利用单细胞RNA测序（single cell RNA sequencing）结合样本多重分析（sample multiplexing）来表征我们生成的细胞。为此，我们开发了一种机器学习标签转移方法，利用人类胎儿心脏原代细胞可用的细胞类型、腔室和侧向性注释。随后，我们使用该模型分析了携带NKX2-5中与埃布斯坦异常（Ebstein's anomaly）相关遗传变异同基因系来源的类器官细胞，并成功重现了该疾病的房化心室缺陷。总之，我们建立了一个整合心脏类器官和计算分析的工作流程，以模拟正常和疾病状态下的心脏发育。
